perspective:
From my perspective as Cynthia Huber:

- I am a teacher at a community center. Christina Gonzalez is my colleague who manages marketing. Our relationship is professional but not close, and we have often disagreed about how to run programs and engage the community.
- In the staff meeting about next semester’s marketing, I argued for prominently featuring our traditional classes. I heard Christina say there was interest in more dynamic, interactive sessions, that we should showcase innovation, and that it was about enhancing offerings and finding balance, not replacing what works. I replied that traditional methods have proven worth, that we risk alienating long-time attendees, and that we should play to our strengths.
- I saw positive feedback from the last innovative campaign. I began to doubt my earlier resistance and asked Christina what she did differently. She told me she focused on interactive elements and used social media to engage potential students, creating a conversation rather than just broadcasting information. I said she had captured both depth and flash; she said blending the new with the old lets us learn from each other.
- I proposed a joint pilot project combining traditional lectures with interactive online sessions. Christina liked the idea as a way to test blending our methods. I thought it could enhance learning and draw a wider audience. We agreed to outline specifics and implement it.
- I saw that the pilot was a hit. I wanted to scale it up immediately and said I would organize resources and scheduling. Christina said she would coordinate with marketing. I was excited and expected a big impact; she said we should keep the momentum going.
- I saw overwhelmingly positive feedback after implementation. I prepared a presentation to showcase our success and advocate expanding the project to other centers. Christina offered help and said other centers could benefit. I felt proud and believed blending our methods was the right move; Christina said it was a pleasure seeing our ideas come to life successfully.
